title: Let a machine work out of her stores: it carries what it cuts, plants from her seed box, and sells at the bin
tier_reason: Sim code behind the unit suite and the replay round-trip; git reverts it. The rules are the design's, set by the CEO's Q-100 table.
ask: WI-9a in docs/V0_2_1_PLAN.md: a robot's harvest goes into its hands (one crop at a time) rather than her basket, so it cannot ship her work; it plants from her seed box and is refused when empty, where a non-player used to plant free; its sell pays the shared per-crop price for the one crop it carries. The observation gains ripe, crow and bin channels and carrying, seeds and bin-offset scalars (207 numbers); the reward table becomes the CEO's eight rows.
source_message: CEO on Q-100, 2026-09-09, chief of staff session: the full reward table.
result: Landed on main (commit 06bd86e merged as part of bf533ac): sim_world.gd's three machine rules with _is_machine/_hands_of, game_state.gd's shared crop_price and sell_one_crop, the 207-number observation with a cached bin lookup, the eight-row Rewards.TABLE; test_machine_economy (23 assertions), test_observation at 41. Unit 2411, integration 671, robot session and gateway green. Left for the brain worker: the learning gate is printed rather than asserted until the tap-shaped brain lands, and farm.gd's verb cues have no plant or sell row yet. The worker also caught that the chief of staff's scripted edit had truncated the plan file; it is rebuilt. Chief of staff verified: ran both suites on main after the merge.

follow_ups.title: Give a machine's planting and selling the same sound and visuals the player gets
follow_ups.first_action: In world/farm.gd, add plant and sell rows to the verb cue table so a non-player actor's PLANT and SELL actions play the same effect and sound the player's do; extend the integration test that watches actor cues to cover both.
follow_ups.why: A machine can now plant from the seed box and sell at the bin, and both currently happen with no cue at all.

follow_ups.title: Make the learning check fail the tests when a robot stops learning
follow_ups.first_action: Once the tap-shaped brain lands, replace the printed learning comparison in the v0.2.1 learning test with an assertion on the same numbers demo_learning_robot.gd prints, and record the chosen threshold in docs/V0_2_1_PLAN.md.
follow_ups.why: The learning result is currently only printed, so a regression in the robot's learning would pass silently.

follow_ups.title: Fix the script that truncated the v0.2.1 plan file
follow_ups.first_action: Find the scripted edit that rewrote docs/V0_2_1_PLAN.md and cut sections four to nine, make it fail loudly instead of writing a shorter file, and check no other plan or design doc lost content the same way.
follow_ups.why: The same script will be used on the next plan edit and will truncate it again.

recommend.question: Do the missing plant and sell cues block a machine doing either in front of the player, or are they a follow-up?
recommend.answer: Treat them as blocking — no machine plants or sells where the player can see it until the cues land.
recommend.why: Our standing rule is that any actor's action the player watches gets the player's own sound and visual treatment, and a silent sale is the clearest way to break that.
recommend.instead: Ship the behaviour now and add cues in the next pass, which gets the economy in front of playtesters sooner but with a machine that acts invisibly.
